title: AI security agent finds a root-access flaw hidden behind a 403 response
friendlyTitle: An AI security tool found that a rejected request could still run code as root
summary: Vulnetic reports that its Sable agent found a OneDev vulnerability where server-side validation compiled attacker-controlled Groovy before an administrator check ran. A low-privilege request received a 403 response yet could still execute code as root, and the researchers say they reported the issue to maintainers.
friendlySummary: Vulnetic’s agent found a flaw in OneDev. The server said access was denied, but it had already processed dangerous code before checking permission.
whyItMatters: A rejected HTTP response does not prove that nothing happened behind it. Security reviews should trace validation and deserialization that run before authorization, while AI-generated findings still need controlled reproduction and coordinated disclosure by people.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Security teams should check what a server does before it rejects a request. AI can help find the path, but people must verify and report the flaw safely.
